# Tagcast 1.2.0 — Your colours, your music

Tagcast 1.2.0 adds custom colour themes and reviewed music uploads, makes repeated
library responses faster, and improves the desktop sign-in experience. The macOS
downloads are now Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple.

## Make Tagcast your own

Open **Settings → Appearance**, or **Theme → Edit themes…**, to create a theme
from any built-in palette. Adjust colours beside a live component preview, with
separate Light and Dark variants and contrast guidance. Changes stay in the
preview until you save. Built-in palettes remain available.

Use **Export JSON** to share a theme or keep a backup, and **Import JSON…** to
open a shared theme as a new unsaved preview. Theme files contain no account or
library information. Saved themes stay local to your browser or desktop profile.
See the illustrated [Custom themes guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki/Custom-themes),
including the downloadable Amber · Original theme inspired by ibfetch.

## Add local music to iBroadcast

Music uploads are optional and **off by default**. Enable them under **Settings →
Data & exports**, save, then reconnect once to approve iBroadcast's upload permission.
On the **Uploads** page, choose local files or a folder, prepare and review the
selection, then choose **Start uploads**. Preparation sends no audio.

Files upload one at a time. Byte-identical files are skipped, progress is grouped
by source folder, and Pause and Stop controls remain available. A delayed entry
in iBroadcast's uploaded-file list is distinguished from a genuinely uncertain
result. Uncertain uploads are never sent again automatically. Use **Reload library**
after iBroadcast has processed the files to see the new albums.

On Windows, Stop can remain pending while a silent server's current request waits
for a reply or timeout. Later files are not sent. This platform limitation is
documented in the upload guide; it does not trigger an automatic retry.

Original files are never edited, moved or deleted. iBroadcast reads their embedded
tags; edits previously made in Tagcast are not written into those local files.
There is no watch-folder service, automatic synchronization or remote deletion.
The desktop app provides native file/folder pickers; browser use accepts paths on
the computer running Tagcast. See [Music uploads](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki/Music-uploads)
for permission, limits and recovery guidance.

## Less repeated work in large libraries

Tagcast reuses compact album summaries while the same loaded library snapshot is
active. This reduces repeated processing in library responses without weakening
fresh conflict checks or save verification. First loading, network transfers and
iBroadcast's read-back after metadata changes still take time. This is not a
promise that every operation or year edit becomes faster.

## A more convenient desktop app

- **Sign in with iBroadcast** opens iBroadcast in a dedicated, restricted sign-in
  window and returns to Tagcast automatically. The device code/browser link remain
  available as a fallback; passwords stay on iBroadcast.
- Desktop window dimensions are remembered for the next launch.
- The sidebar shows the number of your playlists.
- Decade pages have refreshed musical introductions from the 1900s to the 2020s.

## Upgrading and platform support

Quit the old app before opening 1.2.0. Existing settings, credentials, favourites
and preferences are retained. Downloads are available for macOS Apple Silicon and
Intel, Windows x64 and Linux x64, each with a SHA-256 companion. macOS requires
Ventura 13 or newer; Linux requires a compatible graphical desktop.

The player, queue and metadata review/save workflow retain their existing behaviour.
Experimental Gapless playback remains optional and off by default, with its existing
compatible-album scope and ordinary-playback fallback. This release does not add
crossfade or a universal gapless guarantee. Python/browser use remains supported.

## Code signing policy and privacy

The **macOS downloads are Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple**, with the
signature, stapled ticket and Gatekeeper assessment checked after extraction.
Windows downloads are **not yet Authenticode signed**: the SignPath application
is pending and signing is not active. See the [Code signing policy](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast#code-signing-policy)
and [Privacy policy](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v1.2.0/PRIVACY.md).
iBroadcast continues to control account limits, track availability and Premium access.
